Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year prepay inquiry — scale + Q4 sprint needs

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re planning an aggressive product sprint in Q4 and want predictable inference capacity and cost. The team is considering a 3-year prepay to lock economics and get priority capacity, but we need flexibility for seasonal spikes in year 1 and a clear performance safeguard.

High-level ask from procurement:
- 3-year prepaid commitment (target $2.1M ARR equivalent in year 1 frontload)
- Meaningful term discount vs monthly (looking for double-digit %)
- True-up at each anniversary and a performance safeguard (latency/uptime SLO credits)
- Ability to re-profile usage between years (within a defined ramp band)

Can you share a proposal that includes a frontloaded first-year credit, a ramp schedule (year-over-year % allowed reprofile), and an outline of SLA credit mechanics? We’ll need an internal approval path so the doc has to be saleable to procurement & (finance).

Anna
Anna Park
Head of Platform
Orpheus Analytics


From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Anna Park <anna@orpheus.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay inquiry — scale + Q4 sprint needs

Hi Anna —

Appreciate the clarity. I put together a structured proposal attached (Orpheus_3yr_proposal_v1.pdf) and a simple financial model (orpheus_financial_model_v1.xlsx) so you can play with frontload and ramp mechanics. Topline summary here: 

Proposal highlights (draft):
- Commitment: 3 years, $5.8M total committed spend (frontloaded allocation: $2.1M in year 1)
- Term discount: 12% off our list hosted rates applied to committed units
- Ramp/reprofile: allowed +/-20% reprofile between adjacent years without penalty; true-up at each anniversary for overage at committed list rates
- Frontload incentive: additional 3% one-time credit applied in year 1 if frontload >= 35% of total commit
- SLA safeguard: uptime target 99.9%; credit mechanism for sustained miss (>30m window) capped at 3% of monthly committed spend; automatic fallback to compatible model variants during regional capacity stress
- Early termination / clawback: standard pro-rata clawback with a modest stepdown (see section 6) — we kept it simple for procurement review

Next steps I suggest: if you like the framework I’ll route to finance for an executable term sheet and ask for an exception approval for the frontload credit + ramp band. If procurement needs different ramp bands (e.g., +/- 10% instead of 20%) let me know and I’ll include options.

Can we aim for a procurement review by Thu so we can get to an internal approval path next week?

Thanks,
Lauren

Laurens / Karthik —

I reviewed the ask with RevOps. We can approve the following with an exec exception:

- 12% term discount on committed units for hosted usage (applied after any usage-based surcharges).
- Frontload incentive: approve the additional 3% credit if year-1 frontload >= 35% (credit applied as a billing credit in month 2).
- Ramp band: keep +/-20% between adjacent years but add a one-time flexibility carve-out: 1 allowed overage reprofile up to +30% in year 2 only, subject to capacity confirmation.
- True-up/clawback: true-up at each anniversary; any cumulative shortfall at contract end triggers pro-rata clawback at list rates less a 5% amortization allowance.
- SLA credits: approve the 99.9% target; we cap SLA credits at 3% monthly committed spend and require measurement window to be validated by Ops before payout.

Two asks back from RevOps:
1) Add a 90-day notice requirement for any year-to-year reprofile that increases committed consumption > +20% to give us scheduling lead time.
2) Mark the stepdown clawback schedule in the term sheet to be a simple pro-rata (no additional penalties) — RevOps prefers cleaner language.

If you can incorporate these edits into the term sheet I’ll sign off and we can route to legal for a quick review.

Vivek

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the fast feedback and for walking procurement through the objectives. We have internal approval for the structure and a few guardrails (see excerpt below). I attached the final term sheet (approved_term_sheet_ORPHEUS_3yr_vfinal.pdf) for signature. Key agreed points: 

- Commitment: 3 years, $5.8M total committed spend; year-1 frontload $2.1M (meets >=35% frontload threshold).
- Pricing: 12% term discount on committed units (hosted API list), applied monthly to consumption up to committed units.
- Frontload credit: 3% one-time credit applied to month-2 billing if frontload threshold met.
- Ramp/reprofile: +/-20% allowed between adjacent years without penalty. One-time discretionary reprofile up to +30% in year 2 allowed but requires 90-day notice and capacity confirmation.
- True-up & clawback: anniversary true-ups; final cumulative shortfall triggers pro-rata clawback at list rates less 5% amortization allowance.
- SLA: 99.9% monthly target; payout mechanics validated by Ops; cap at 3% of monthly committed spend.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached term sheet. If acceptable, sign via DocuSign link (included).
2) Once signed, Legal will send the final SOW template and we’ll schedule a kickoff to reserve dedicated capacity for your Q4 sprint.

I’ll leave Vivek & Karthik copied for any post-signature billing routing. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if procurement wants to walk the changes live.

Best,
